simple.meaning: מֵאָה (mêʼâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a hundred ; also as a multiplicative and a fraction.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 583 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, beginning at Genesis 5:3. Its contexts include family, family line, death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֵאָה (H3967).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מֵאָה (mêʼâh) / H3967 is traced through Genesis 5:3, Genesis 5:4, Genesis 5:5, Genesis 5:6 as a generated source-based concept entry.

H). c. absolute plural ׃מֵא(וֺ)ת — (1) alone, = hundreds , לְמֵאוֺת 1Sam 29:2 by hundreds , so 2Sam 18:4 (both + thousands); especially (הַ)מּ ׳שָׂרֵי captains of (the) hundreds Exod 18:21 , 25 (E), 2Kin 11:4 , 9 , 10 , 15 +; (2) multiplied, followed by noun enumerated, in singular: מ ׳שְׁלשׁ אִישׁ Judg 7:6 , 300 men , compare 7:7 ; 7:8 ; 7:16 ; 8:4 ; Exod 12:27 (E), etc.; מ ׳אַרְבַּע שָׁנָה Gen 15:13 (JE) 400 years ; מ ׳חֲמֵשׁ אֶלֶף 2Sam 24:9 500, 000 , compare 2Chr 13:17 ; מ ׳שֵׁשׁ רֶכֶב Exod 14:7 (J) 600 chariots ; ׳מ שְׁבַע אִישׁ Judg 20:15-16 , 700 men ; מ ׳שְׁמֹנֶה חָלָל 2Sam 23:8 800 slain ; מ ׳תְּשַׁע רֶכֶב Judg 4:3 , 13 900 chariots ; (3) less often followed by plural noun: מ ׳שְׁלשׁ שׁוּעָלִים 15:4 300 foxes ; מ ׳חֲמֵשׁ אֲתוֺנוֺת Job 1:3 500 she-asses , etc.; (4) rare, and chiefly late, after plural noun מ שְׁלשׁ ׳מִּלַגְשִׁים 1Kin 11:3 300 concubines , compare 7:42 2Chr 4:13 ; 1Chr 4:42 ; 2Chr 14:8 etc.; after n.collective מ חֲמֵשׁ ׳בָּקָר 35:9 ; (5) rare is מ ׳חֲמֵשׁ בַּשֶּׁקֶל Exod 30:24 (P); (6) ellipsis of n., מ ׳שְׁלשׁ כֶּסֶף Gen 45:22 (E), etc. d. construct singular, only followed by singular, and late: מְאַתשָֿׁנָה Gen 11:10 ; 21:5 ; 25:7 (all P) + 25 t. Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters came on the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the sky’s windows opened.
The waters flooded the earth one hundred fifty days.
The waters continually receded from the earth. After the end of one hundred fifty days the waters receded.

In the six hundred first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ship, and looked. He saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
Noah lived three hundred fifty years after the flood.
All the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, and then he died.
This is the history of the generations of Shem: Shem was one hundred years old when he became the father of Arpachshad two years after the flood.
Shem lived five hundred years after he became the father of Arpachshad, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Arpachshad lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Shelah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Shelah lived four hundred three years after he became the father of Eber, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Eber lived four hundred thirty years after he became the father of Peleg, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Peleg lived two hundred nine years after he became the father of Reu, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Reu lived two hundred seven years after he became the father of Serug, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Serug lived two hundred years after he became the father of Nahor, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
Nahor lived one hundred nineteen years after he became the father of Terah, and became the father of more sons and daughters.
The days of Terah were two hundred five years. Terah died in Haran.

Then Abraham fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, “Will a child be born to him who is one hundred years old? Will Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?”
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years. This was the length of Sarah’s life.

thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.

He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.
The days of Isaac were one hundred eighty years.
He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.

So Joseph died, being one hundred ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

and he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, with captains over all of them.
